title: Boothie made $208K in five months by riding the digicam selfie trend on TikTok
dek: A two-person team launched an AI selfie app in June 2026, aimed it at people already posting on TikTok, and passed $56K in a single month by October. Then they put it up for sale.

phases.name: A simpler app first?
phases.story: In April 2025 a free iPhone app also called Boothie appeared: a plain vintage photobooth that takes three shots and makes a photo strip, with no AI. It came from a different developer account, and its code is public on GitHub. We couldn't confirm it is the same team, so treat this as a maybe.
phases.lesson: A small free version is a cheap way to test a name and an idea before you add the expensive part.

phases.name: Launch into a trend
phases.story: The AI app launched on June 23, 2026. You pick a look, like a 2000s digicam flash, Kodak film or a vintage photobooth, take a selfie, and get it back in that style. The basic editor is free. The AI looks cost credits, through weekly subscriptions or credit packs. It earned $4,727 in its first week.
phases.lesson: When a look is already trending, a tool that makes that exact look in one tap is easy to explain.

phases.name: TikTok does the selling
phases.story: The app is aimed at women 16 to 40 who post on TikTok and Instagram, and TikTok is its only listed marketing channel. A sale listing says growth came from TikTok photo carousels (posts you swipe through) posted by almost a dozen accounts in the US, Germany and Turkey. The website even tells visitors how to escape TikTok's built-in browser to reach the App Store. Revenue jumped to $27,283 in July and $43,716 in August.
phases.lesson: Show the before and after where your customer already scrolls. If your posts come from made-up characters, say so, or you risk losing trust and breaking the platform's rules.

phases.name: Android and the best month
phases.story: An Android version came out on Google Play in September 2026, and a proper website went up by early October. October was the best month so far at $56,432.
phases.lesson: Once one platform works, the next one can add customers without new marketing.

phases.name: Selling the business
phases.story: On October 9, 2026, about 15 weeks after launch, Boothie was listed for sale on TrustMRR. The asking price there is $900,000, and it had received 32 offers. A different site lists it at $2,000,000. Trend apps can fade fast, so some founders sell while the numbers are high. In November the same developer account released a new app, a photo cleaner called Swipezy.
phases.lesson: An app is an asset: if you build something that earns, someone may pay you for it.

fact_checks.who: Sale listing on whatsthe.app (author not named)
fact_checks.found: Verified revenue was $43,416 in September 2026, so $38K MRR fits. But the same page shows 1,402 active subscriptions, and TrustMRR shows 2,401 in November. 8,200 paying users doesn't match.
fact_checks.label: Sources differ

fact_checks.found: TrustMRR lists TikTok as the only marketing channel, and a sale listing says growth came from TikTok carousels posted by almost a dozen accounts.
fact_checks.label: Sources differ

fact_checks.claim: "A six-figure business within months of launch"
fact_checks.found: TrustMRR shows $208,574 all-time revenue by Nov 18 2026, about five months after the June 23 launch. The monthly numbers already passed $100,000 before November, when the claim was made.
fact_checks.label: Verified

wayback.headline: Turn one selfie into the photos you keep saving
wayback.sub: Pick a look, snap a selfie, and Boothie restyles it in seconds.
wayback.prices: Free to download; AI photos use credits (Boothie Plus and Gold include daily credits, plus credit packs)

checklist: Scroll TikTok or Instagram for 20 minutes and write down three looks or formats you keep seeing.
Pick one and ask: could a tool make this in one tap? Sketch the before and after.
Make one free thing people can use, and one paid thing that is clearly better.
Post three before-and-after carousels from your own account and track which one gets saved most.
If people find you through TikTok, test that your link actually opens from inside the TikTok app.
Look up what similar apps sell for on TrustMRR to see what a working app can be worth.
